theme: General Knowledge Vol 12: Lost Civilizations, Deep Time & Modern Technology
title: General Knowledge Vol 12: Lost Civilizations, Deep Time & Modern Technology
description: A 60-question grand master assessment exploring ancient astronomy, seafloor spreading, Renaissance anatomy, mass extinctions, microprocessors, world deserts, perspective art, fluid mechanics, writing systems, and Mars exploration.

questions.question: What ancient Greek analog computer recovered from a shipwreck in 1901 used bronze gear trains to calculate planetary positions and eclipses?
questions.explanation: Dated to roughly 150 to 100 BCE, the Antikythera mechanism used over thirty interlocking bronze gears to track the Metonic and Saros cycles.

questions.question: Which ancient Mesoamerican civilization developed the sophisticated Long Count calendar system tracking time in cycles of 144,000 days (b'ak'tuns)?
questions.explanation: The Maya recorded astronomical solar, lunar, and Venusian synodic cycles on stone stelae and codices with exceptional mathematical accuracy.

questions.question: Which ancient Greek astronomer of Samos was the first known scholar to propose a comprehensive heliocentric model of the solar system around 270 BCE?
questions.explanation: Aristarchus calculated relative distances and sizes of the Sun and Moon, deducing that the immense Sun must sit at the center of planetary orbits.

questions.question: Which ancient Mesopotamian clay cuneiform tablet records detailed astronomical observations of the planet Venus during the reign of King Ammisaduqa?
questions.explanation: The tablet recorded first and last risings of Venus over twenty-one years, providing modern historians with critical chronological anchors for Babylon.

questions.question: Which ancient Greek astronomer invented trigonometry, created the first comprehensive star catalog, and discovered the precession of the equinoxes?
questions.explanation: Hipparchus compared star positions with records made 150 years earlier by Timocharis, noting stars had shifted eastward by approximately one degree per century.

questions.question: How many days comprised the solar agricultural year (Haab') in the ancient Maya calendar system?
questions.imperialDisplay: 365 days (18 months of 20 days plus 5 Wayeb days)
questions.explanation: The Maya Haab' calendar consisted of eighteen named months of twenty days each, plus a final unlucky period of five days called Wayeb'.

questions.question: Which American geologist and naval officer proposed the theory of Seafloor Spreading in 1960, showing new oceanic crust forms at mid-ocean ridges?
questions.explanation: Hess used sonar sounding data to show that magma wells up at mid-ocean ridges and spreads laterally, conveyor-belting ocean crust toward trenches.

questions.question: What is the longest mountain range on Earth, a continuous volcanic ridge system stretching over 65,000 kilometers across the global ocean floor?
questions.explanation: The Mid-Ocean Ridge winds through the Atlantic, Indian, and Pacific Oceans, forming new oceanic basaltic lithosphere at divergent boundaries.

questions.question: What term describes flat-topped underwater volcanic seamounts that were eroded by wave action at sea level before subsiding into the abyss?
questions.explanation: Harry Hess named these flat-topped underwater mountains guyots after Swiss-American geographer Arnold Henry Guyot.

questions.question: What geological process occurs where dense oceanic plates sink beneath lighter continental or younger oceanic plates into the mantle?
questions.explanation: Subduction zones produce the world deepest ocean trenches, powerful megathrust earthquakes, and volcanic island arcs.

questions.question: What deep oceanic trench in the northwestern Pacific off Kamchatka and the Kuril Islands reaches depths exceeding 10,500 meters?
questions.explanation: Formed where the Pacific Plate subducts under the Okhotsk Plate, the Kuril-Kamchatka Trench is among the deepest ocean chasms on Earth.

questions.question: What is the approximate total length in kilometers of the global Mid-Ocean Ridge mountain system across the ocean basins?
questions.explanation: The interconnected mid-ocean ridge system spans approximately 65,000 kilometers across Earth ocean basins.

questions.question: Which Flemish anatomist published the landmark masterwork De humani corporis fabrica in 1543, revolutionizing medicine with accurate human dissections?
questions.explanation: Vesalius conducted direct human dissections in Padua, correcting over two hundred anatomical errors taught for centuries from Galen animal dissections.

questions.question: Which English physician published De Motu Cordis in 1628, providing the first complete description of the systemic circulation of blood pumped by the heart?
questions.explanation: Harvey calculated that the heart pumps more blood in an hour than the body weight, proving blood must circulate continuously through a closed arterial-venous loop.

questions.question: Which Italian physician and biologist used a microscope in 1661 to discover microscopic capillaries, bridging Harvey arteries and veins?
questions.explanation: Malpighi examined frog lungs under magnification, identifying the tiny capillary vessels where oxygen and nutrient gas exchange takes place.

questions.question: Which Italian Renaissance polymath created hundreds of exceptionally detailed anatomical sketches based on thirty human dissections between 1500 and 1515?
questions.explanation: Leonardo collaborated with anatomist Marcantonio della Torre, illustrating the aortic valve, coronary vessels, and biomechanics with unprecedented precision.

questions.question: Which Dutch cloth merchant and microscopist first observed living single-celled bacteria and protozoa, calling them animalcules in 1676?
questions.explanation: Leeuwenhoek ground high-power single-sphere glass lenses achieving over 200x magnification, discovering spermatozoa, red blood cells, and oral microbes.

questions.question: In what year did Andreas Vesalius publish his revolutionary anatomical treatise De humani corporis fabrica in Basel?
questions.explanation: Published in 1543 (the same year as Copernicus De revolutionibus), Vesalius work transformed medicine into an empirical observational science.

questions.question: Which catastrophic mass extinction event 252 million years ago wiped out roughly 96 percent of all marine species and 70 percent of terrestrial vertebrates?
questions.explanation: Massive volcanic eruptions from the Siberian Traps released trillions of tons of carbon dioxide, triggering extreme ocean acidification and anoxia.

questions.question: Which fossil-rich Canadian Rocky Mountain shale formation preserved soft-bodied marine organisms from the Cambrian Explosion 508 million years ago?
questions.explanation: Discovered by Charles Walcott in 1909, the Burgess Shale revealed bizarre stem-group arthropods like Anomalocaris, Opabinia, and Hallucigenia.

questions.question: What famous natural asphalt seep in Los Angeles, California, has preserved hundreds of thousands of Ice Age mammal fossils like smilodons and mammoths?
questions.explanation: Naturally bubbling crude oil formed sticky asphalt traps over fifty thousand years, preserving the dense skeletal remains of dire wolves and saber-toothed cats.

questions.question: During which geological period 359 to 299 million years ago did massive lycopsid tree swamps accumulate, forming most of Earth coal beds?
questions.explanation: Lignin-rich trees grew in vast wetlands with few fungi capable of decomposing them, burying organic carbon and elevating atmospheric oxygen to thirty-five percent.

questions.question: What geological era, spanning from 541 million years ago to the present, is characterized by abundant macroscopic, multicellular fossil life?
questions.explanation: The Phanerozoic (meaning visible life) comprises the Paleozoic, Mesozoic, and Cenozoic eras, marked by the emergence of hard shells and bones.

questions.question: What percentage of marine species were wiped out during the Permian-Triassic mass extinction (The Great Dying)?
questions.explanation: The Permian-Triassic extinction event was the deadliest in Earth history, destroying an estimated 96 percent of all marine species.

questions.question: Which four-bit microprocessor released by Intel in 1971, designed by Federico Faggin and Ted Hoff, was the world first commercial single-chip CPU?
questions.explanation: The Intel 4004 contained 2,300 transistors on a single silicon die, designed originally for the Japanese Busicom electronic desktop printing calculator.

questions.question: Which computer architecture design, formulated by John von Neumann in 1945, stores both program instructions and data in the same shared memory space?
questions.explanation: Von Neumann architecture forms the foundation of modern general-purpose computers, utilizing a central processor, arithmetic logic unit, registers, and unified memory.

questions.question: Which British mathematician introduced the theoretical concept of a universal computing machine with a tape and read-write head in 1936?
questions.explanation: Turing landmark paper On Computable Numbers proved fundamental limits on algorithmic computability and founded theoretical computer science.

questions.question: Which American computer scientist and US Navy Rear Admiral developed the first compiler in 1952 and helped develop the COBOL programming language?
questions.explanation: Grace Hopper coined the term compiler for translating English-like programming language statements into machine code, pioneering user-friendly software.

questions.question: Which solid-state device invented in 1959 at Bell Labs by Mohamed Atalla and Dawon Kahng became the most widely manufactured device in human history?
questions.explanation: The Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor Field-Effect Transistor (MOSFET) is the basic switching element in modern microprocessors, with trillions built daily.

questions.question: In what year did Intel release the 4004, the world first commercial single-chip microprocessor?
questions.explanation: Intel officially advertised the 4004 in Electronic News on November 15, 1971, launching the microcomputer revolution.

questions.question: Which cold winter desert in northern China and southern Mongolia is famous for the 1920s discovery of the first fossilized dinosaur eggs by Roy Chapman Andrews?
questions.explanation: The Gobi Desert Flaming Cliffs (Bayanzag) yielded Protoceratops skulls, Velociraptor skeletons, and the first confirmed dinosaur nests in paleontology.

questions.question: What immense sand sea covering roughly 650,000 square kilometers on the southern Arabian Peninsula is known as the Empty Quarter?
questions.explanation: The Rub' al Khali is the world largest continuous sand desert, featuring barchan and longitudinal dunes rising over 250 meters high.

questions.question: Which large semi-arid sandy savanna in southern Africa spanning Botswana, Namibia, and South Africa is the ancestral homeland of the San people?
questions.explanation: The Kalahari is technically a semi-desert with seasonal rainfall, supporting diverse wildlife like meerkats, gemsbok, and black-maned Kalahari lions.

questions.question: What is the largest hot desert in the world, covering approximately 9.2 million square kilometers across North Africa?
questions.explanation: The Sahara encompasses vast rocky plateaus (hamada), gravel plains (reg), and undulating sand seas (erg), spanning from the Atlantic Ocean to the Red Sea.

questions.question: Which desert spanning the northwestern Indian state of Rajasthan and eastern Pakistan is the most densely populated desert on Earth?
questions.explanation: The Great Indian Desert has an average population density of eighty-three people per square kilometer, home to rich cultural traditions and vibrant camel fairs.

questions.question: What is the approximate total area in millions of square kilometers covered by the Sahara Desert across North Africa?
questions.explanation: The Sahara Desert covers roughly 9.2 million square kilometers, an area comparable in size to the entire United States or China.

questions.question: Which Italian master painted the monumental ceiling frescoes of the Sistine Chapel in Rome between 1508 and 1512 under the patronage of Pope Julius II?
questions.explanation: Michelangelo spent four years painting while standing upright on custom wooden scaffolding, completing iconic scenes like The Creation of Adam.

questions.question: Which Florentine architect demonstrated the mathematical principles of linear perspective around 1415 using mirrors and the Florence Baptistery?
questions.explanation: Brunelleschi showed how orthogonal lines converge at a single vanishing point on the horizon line, creating a convincing illusion of 3D depth on a flat surface.

questions.question: Which High Renaissance master painted The School of Athens in the Vatican Papal Palace, depicting Plato, Aristotle, and classical philosophers in an ideal hall?
questions.explanation: Raphael incorporated portraits of contemporary Renaissance rivals into ancient philosophers, modeling Plato on Leonardo da Vinci and Heraclitus on Michelangelo.

questions.question: Which late Renaissance and Baroque master revolutionized European oil painting with dramatic theatrical contrast between bright light and dark shadows (chiaroscuro)?
questions.explanation: Caravaggio used extreme dark backgrounds (tenebrism) and raw realism in works like The Calling of Saint Matthew and The Incredulity of Saint Thomas.

questions.question: On the refectory wall of which Dominican convent in Milan did Leonardo da Vinci paint his famous mural The Last Supper between 1495 and 1498?
questions.explanation: Leonardo used experimental tempera on dry gesso rather than true wet buon fresco, creating a luminous masterpiece that began deteriorating during his lifetime.

questions.question: In what year did Michelangelo complete and unveil the painted ceiling of the Sistine Chapel in Rome?
questions.explanation: Pope Julius II held an inaugural Mass under Michelangelo newly completed ceiling on All Saints Day, November 1, 1512.

questions.question: Which Swiss mathematician and physicist published Hydrodynamica in 1738, formulating the principle that fluid pressure decreases as flow velocity increases?
questions.explanation: Bernoulli principle explains pressure differentials that contribute to aerodynamic lift, carburetor fuel intake, and venturi flowmeters.

questions.question: What dimensionless quantity in fluid mechanics predicts whether fluid flow will be smooth and laminar or chaotic and turbulent?
questions.explanation: Named after Osborne Reynolds, it calculates the ratio of inertial forces to viscous forces within a moving fluid.

questions.question: Which Austrian physicist and philosopher gave his name to the ratio of an object speed through a fluid medium to the local speed of sound?
questions.explanation: Mach 1 represents local sonic velocity, Mach numbers above one are supersonic, and speeds above Mach 5 are classified as hypersonic.

questions.question: What aerodynamic phenomenon causes a moving fluid jet to stay attached to a convex curved surface rather than traveling in a straight line?
questions.explanation: Discovered by Romanian aerodynamicist Henri Coandă in 1910, this effect is utilized in lift-enhancing aircraft flaps and high-lift airfoils.

questions.question: What physical effect causes a spinning ball or cylinder moving through air to curve away from its initial trajectory due to pressure differences?
questions.explanation: Heinrich Gustav Magnus described how boundary layer friction on the advancing side of a spinning sphere accelerates airflow, generating lateral deflection.

questions.question: In what year did Daniel Bernoulli publish his foundational treatise Hydrodynamica in Strasbourg?
questions.explanation: Daniel Bernoulli formulated conservation of energy for flowing fluids in Hydrodynamica, published in 1738.

questions.question: What ancient wedge-shaped script developed in Sumer around 3400 BCE was pressed into wet clay tablets with a reed stylus?
questions.explanation: Cuneiform evolved from pictographic accounting tokens into a logo-syllabic script used across Mesopotamia for over three thousand years.

questions.question: Which ancient maritime trading civilization developed the first widespread consonantal alphabet (abjad) around 1050 BCE, ancestor to Greek and Latin?
questions.explanation: The Phoenician alphabet of twenty-two consonants simplified writing by representing phonetic sounds rather than thousands of complex logograms.

questions.question: Which Cherokee polymath and silversmith independently created a complete eighty-five-character syllabary for the Cherokee language in 1821?
questions.explanation: Sequoyah achievement enabled the Cherokee Nation to achieve over ninety percent literacy within years and publish the bilingual Cherokee Phoenix newspaper.

questions.question: What mysterious glyphic writing system etched onto wooden rongo-rongo tablets on Easter Island remains undeciphered by modern linguists?
questions.explanation: Rongorongo tablets use reverse boustrophedon reading order, where lines alternate orientation, requiring the tablet to be rotated 180 degrees every line.

questions.question: Which Bronze Age writing system used in the Indus River Valley cities of Mohenjo-daro and Harappa remains undeciphered due to lack of bilingual inscriptions?
questions.explanation: Found on thousands of small steatite stamp seals, Indus script consists of over four hundred distinct signs with typical inscriptions averaging only five symbols.

questions.question: How many total phonetic characters made up the Cherokee syllabary created by Sequoyah in 1821?
questions.explanation: Sequoyah's Cherokee syllabary consists of 85 distinct characters representing every consonant-vowel syllable in the spoken Cherokee tongue.

questions.question: Which robotic NASA spacecraft achieved the first successful Mars soft landing by an American probe on July 20, 1976, returning the first color panoramas?
questions.explanation: Viking 1 operated on Chryse Planitia for over six years, conducting biological soil tests, atmospheric measurements, and weather tracking.

questions.question: Which SUV-sized NASA rover landed inside Gale Crater on Mars in August 2012 using an innovative rocket-powered Sky Crane descent stage?
questions.explanation: Curiosity discovered mudstones deposited in ancient freshwater lakebeds, confirming Mars had environmental conditions capable of supporting microbial life.

questions.question: Which small robotic coaxial helicopter achieved the first powered controlled flight on another planet inside Jezero Crater on Mars in April 2021?
questions.explanation: Ingenuity completed seventy-two successful flights over three years, serving as an aerial scout for the Perseverance rover across Martian terrain.

questions.question: Which Japanese robotic spacecraft returned the first subsurface samples from a carbonaceous near-Earth asteroid (Ryugu) to Earth in 2020?
questions.explanation: JAXA Hayabusa2 fired a tantalum impactor into Ryugu to collect pristine subsurface rubble containing amino acids and organic compounds.

questions.question: Which European Space Agency mission became the first spacecraft to rendezvous with and orbit a comet (67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko) in 2014?
questions.explanation: Rosetta deployed the Philae lander onto the comet surface and accompanied the comet through perihelion, analyzing organic gases and ice composition.

questions.question: In what year did the Viking 1 lander touch down on the surface of Mars?
questions.explanation: Viking 1 touched down safely on Mars on July 20, 1976, transmitting the first close-up surface photographs from another planet.
